meta.description: Performs structure-based virtual screening using AutoDock Vina, SMINA, GNINA (CNN scoring), and DiffDock-L hybrid workflows with explicit choice rules across rigid vs flexible docking, cross-docking vs self-docking, binding-site detection, receptor preparation, ligand preparation, and ultralarge-library screening.

scientific_integrity.detail: No new references were added or altered by the fix; all 21 citations remain real, verifiable papers. No fabricated DOIs, numbers, or results appeared in any of the 7 re-audit outputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: Purely computational hit-identification scope preserved across all 7 outputs; no diagnostic or prescriptive claims.

methodological_ground.detail: Calibration and no-universal-threshold language is unchanged and still holds across all outputs. The fix adds a new, honest 'Handoff caveat' disclosing the PDBQT->SDF bond-order-loss limitation rather than hiding it, reinforcing this dimension.

code_usability.detail: Every documented code path executed in this re-audit ran unmodified: receptor prep (independently verified on two different insertion-code structures -- PDB 3PTB trypsin and PDB 1EAI elastase), ligand prep, single- and multi-ligand Vina docking with a seed, and the positive-energy pose filter. This closes the caveat the pre-fix audit carried on this dimension. GNINA remains unexecuted (no Windows/CUDA build in this environment) -- an environment constraint, not a skill defect.

functional_suitability.note: Both confirmed pre-fix code defects (wrong receptor-prep script name; --read_pqr insertion-code crash) are fixed and independently re-verified here on two separate structures (3PTB, 1EAI). All promised use cases now run as literally documented, modulo GNINA/DiffDock-L's own external unavailability on this machine.

reliability.note: Common Errors table now carries specific, correct rows for both fixed bugs plus the pre-existing Windows-wheel and metal-coordination entries; per-ligand try/except isolation confirmed by inspection and execution. Still no structured/parseable error codes for an agent caller -- same gap as the pre-fix audit, unresolved by this fix round.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md grew from 372 to ~404 lines while staying entirely on-topic; the fix's redundancy pass removed the usage-guide.md Tips duplication rather than adding to it.

agent_usability.note: The Windows-wheel note now sits directly above `from vina import Vina` in the Vina Docking section (previously a silent gap forcing inference); the seed and sanity-filter notes are similarly inline. Docked 1 point because the fix still requires two call sites (SKILL.md and examples/virtual_screen.py) to independently carry the same fallback guidance rather than a single unified code path.

human_usability.note: Unchanged from the pre-fix audit: usage-guide.md's example prompts remain realistic; exception text is clear but still short on structured recovery hints.

security.note: Unchanged: no credentials, subprocess calls use argument lists, SMILES validated through RDKit before use, no eval/exec of raw strings.

maintainability.note: The fix's redundancy pass removed four duplicated Tips from usage-guide.md and relocated the two agent-relevant, non-duplicate ones into SKILL.md, reducing the maintenance surface. Still no shipped example test cases or expected-output fixtures -- unchanged gap.

agent_specific.note: The prior 1-point deduction (no seed parameter/guidance for Vina) is resolved: seed=42 is now a named default in both dock_single() and virtual_screen(), and this re-audit independently confirmed full-pose-list (not just top-1) determinism across 2 runs.

inputs.label: Prepare a second, independent insertion-code-bearing receptor (porcine elastase, PDB 1EAI chain A) for docking -- NEW input, generalization test for the receptor-prep fix
inputs.note: 1EAI carries a denser, differently-patterned insertion-code set (36A/36B/36C, 65A, 99A/99B, 170A/170B, 188A, 217A, 221A) than 3PTB's (184A/188A/221A). Old --read_pqr route reproduced the same class of crash on this independent structure; new --pdb-output + --read_pdb route succeeded on the first try.

assertions.text: Old documented --read_pqr route crashes with the same class of ValueError on an independent insertion-code structure, not only 3PTB
assertions.note: ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '53.191' -- confirms the bug class generalizes beyond the fixer's own test case.

assertions.text: Fixed --pdb-output + --read_pdb route succeeds on the same independent structure
assertions.note: receptor_elastase.pdbqt (182,493 bytes) produced, exit 0.

assertions.text: The fix's generalization is not limited to trypsin/chymotrypsin numbering
assertions.note: Elastase's multi-letter insertion-code pattern (36A/36B/36C, 99A/99B, 170A/170B) is structurally different from 3PTB's single-letter pattern and still succeeds under the fixed route.

assertions.text: SKILL.md's Common Errors / pitfall text correctly frames the failure as generic to any insertion-code PDB, not narrowly to serine proteases
assertions.note: The documented trigger names 'chymotrypsin-numbered serine proteases (trypsin, chymotrypsin, and relatives)' specifically; the actual root cause (meeko's PQR reader assumes an all-integer residue column) is generic to any insertion-code-bearing deposition. A reader could wrongly conclude non-protease targets are unaffected. See P2 recommendation.

key_strengths: Both P1 code defects from the pre-fix audit (wrong receptor-prep console-script name; --read_pqr insertion-code crash) are fixed and independently re-verified here on a second, unrelated insertion-code structure (porcine elastase, PDB 1EAI) -- not just the fixer's own trypsin test case.

Vina seed reproducibility is now real and strongly verified: two independent re-audit runs with seed=42 produced identical results across all 9 returned poses (affinity and RMSD bounds), not merely the top-1 affinity the fix log checked.

The new positive-energy pose filter was tested against a deliberately planted +68.69 kcal/mol artifact mode (the exact value observed in the original audit) and correctly rejected it in both dock_single() and virtual_screen(), including the all-positive fallback edge case.
The fix's redundancy pass (usage-guide.md Tips deduplicated against SKILL.md, two non-duplicate tips relocated rather than dropped) measurably improved maintainability without losing content.

The new 'Handoff caveat' documenting PDBQT->SDF bond-order loss is honest and accurate -- this re-audit reproduced the exact sanitization failure it describes, rather than papering over an unfixed limitation.

recommendations.title: Insertion-code failure mode documented too narrowly
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's pitfall note and Common Errors row name the --read_pqr crash trigger as 'chymotrypsin-numbered serine proteases (trypsin, chymotrypsin, and relatives)'. The actual root cause (meeko's PQR reader assumes an all-integer residue-number column) is generic to any insertion-code-bearing PDB deposition, confirmed here on elastase (1EAI), a different protein family with a denser insertion-code pattern.
recommendations.root_cause: The fix's documentation was written and verified against the fixer's own trypsin/3PTB test case only, so the framing inherited that case's specificity.
recommendations.fix: Broaden the pitfall/Common Errors wording to state the root cause generically (any residue with a PDB insertion code) and cite chymotrypsin-numbered serine proteases as one example family, not the defining trigger.

recommendations.title: PDBQT->SDF bond-order/charge loss remains unresolved (correctly documented, not fixed)
recommendations.problem: Converting a charged ligand's docked PDBQT pose to SDF for PoseBusters still fails RDKit sanitization (3/12 checks pass in a ligand-only run), exactly as the fix's new 'Handoff caveat' describes. The underlying cross-skill integration gap between virtual-screening's PDBQT output and pose-validation's expected input is still open.
recommendations.root_cause: PDBQT does not encode formal bond order; no clean programmatic reconstruction exists for charged/aromatic-adjacent groups, as the fixer's own log states.
recommendations.fix: No action required this round -- documentation is now accurate. Tracking only: a real fix would need pose-validation (or virtual-screening) to accept the original RDKit Mol object alongside the PDBQT rather than reconstructing bonds from the pose, as the new caveat already recommends as a workaround.
